### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-defaults/ui.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-defaults/ui.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **153** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **153**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **98** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **136** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 836aad2a19bd4639ded6a3a6bf18db8a75d3a2c3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d8ad5893cd5bf2fe76471fd3e4affd725405e0ed` — the merge of head `72e9a6a027fe4c3279d67ca1d100a4c95bcceb82` into base `836aad2a19bd4639ded6a3a6bf18db8a75d3a2c3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d8ad5893cd5bf2fe76471fd3e4affd725405e0ed && git checkout d8ad5893cd5bf2fe76471fd3e4affd725405e0ed
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 836aad2a19bd4639ded6a3a6bf18db8a75d3a2c3 72e9a6a027fe4c3279d67ca1d100a4c95bcceb82 && git checkout -B drift-repro 836aad2a19bd4639ded6a3a6bf18db8a75d3a2c3 && git merge --no-ff 72e9a6a027fe4c3279d67ca1d100a4c95bcceb82

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 836aad2a19bd4639ded6a3a6bf18db8a75d3a2c3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `72e9a6a027fe4c3279d67ca1d100a4c95bcceb82`

### ① Derived judgments

- **The declaration moved, and only the declaration.** `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts:1109` is `pageSize: z.number().int().positive().default(50).describe(` (was `.default(25)` at merge-base `836aad2a`); the three `describe` lines are diff context, so the describe is byte-identical. The other two `pageSize` defaults in the tree (`kernel/metadata-plugin.zod.ts:400` = 50, `marketplace/marketplace.zod.ts:435` = 20) are untouched, per the card's scope line. Right.
- **Accept set unchanged.** Probe on a throwaway worktree of the head (tsx against `src/ui/view.zod.ts`, then the same with `view.zod.ts` swapped to `origin/main` and restored): `{ pageSize: 0 }` REFUSED `too_small@pageSize`, `{ pageSize: -1 }` REFUSED `too_small@pageSize`, `{ pageSize: 2.5 }` REFUSED `invalid_type@pageSize`, identical before and after. The three refusal pins in `view.test.ts` and `component-object-grid-pagination-accept-set.pin.test.ts` are unedited in the diff. Right.
- **Parsed output: `{}` moves 25 to 50, absence stays absent, authored values survive.** Probe, before / after: `PaginationConfigSchema.parse({})` 25 / 50; `ListViewSchema` with `pagination: {}` 25 / 50; `ListViewSchema` with no `pagination` key: `'pagination' in data` false on both sides (`view.zod.ts:2616` is `PaginationConfigSchema.optional()`, no default); `pagination: { pageSize: 25 }` 25 / 25; `ObjectListViewSchema` behaves the same (`{}` to 50, absent stays absent). The changeset's FROM/TO table and the PR body's three-row parse table say exactly this. Right.
- **Public surface regenerated where it is tracked.** `packages/spec/authorable-defaults/ui.json:85` now reads `ui/PaginationConfig:pageSize = 50`; `content/docs/references/ui/view.mdx:930`, `:1329`, `:1598` (the `ListView.pagination`, `ObjectListView.pagination` and `PaginationConfig` tables) read `optional (default: 50)`. The PR body's "published JSON Schema `json-schema/ui/PaginationConfig.json` now has `default: 50`" is a statement about build output, not a tracked file: `packages/spec/json-schema/` is gitignored (`.gitignore:63`); the tracked witness for that emission is the authorable-defaults row, which the ratchet re-derives from the build. Consistent. Right.
- **By-declaration sweep is complete.** `git grep` at the head over `content/`, `docs/`, `skills/`, `examples/`, `apps/`, `packages/` and the tracked spec sidecars (`docs/`, `prompts/`, `declaration-map/`, `authorable-surface/`, `liveness/`, `api-surface/`) for any text stating 25 as a page-size default: zero hits outside the PR's own new files. Every remaining `pageSize: 25` is an authored value (`plugin-approvals` `sys-approval-request.object.ts` x3, `packages/cli/src/commands/generate.ts:164`, spec tests on other surfaces) and parses to 25 on both sides. The one `.default(25)` left in prose, `component-object-grid-pagination-accept-set.pin.test.ts:14`, sits under the column header `declaration before #19046` (line 12): a historical record, correctly left alone. Right.
- **Test pins.** The default pin flipped to 50; the "custom page size" pin moved its input from 50 to 25 (`view.test.ts:1437-1441` and `:1444-1453`). Necessary, not cosmetic: with a default of 50 an input of 50 could no longer tell "authored value survived" from "default applied". Right.
- **objectui at the pin (`f8a9d0fb05`) does NOT receive the 50 through the schema.** `packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts:146` is `PaginationConfigSchema = stripImportedDefaults(SpecPaginationConfigSchema)`; the walk in `packages/types/src/zod/imported-defaults.ts` removes every `ZodDefault` at the import boundary and re-optionalises (objectui#8317, batch #90), so objectui's validator materialises no page size from the spec before or after this PR. The renderers keep their own numbers today: `plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx:1164` `DEFAULT_FLAT_PAGE_SIZE = 10`, `plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx:962` `DEFAULT_LIST_PAGE_SIZE = 100`, `plugin-kanban/src/ObjectKanban.tsx:85` `DEFAULT_KANBAN_LIMIT = 100`. So 50 reaches the Console only when objectui#9853 makes the renderer read the spec's declared default by a route other than the stripped parse. The changeset says exactly this ("the Console does so once objectui#9853 lands") and the PR body says "objectui#9853 is where the renderer starts reading this default"; nothing in the PR claims a Console effect today. Right. Wording note, not blocking: the new docblock at `view.zod.ts:1100-1103` states the norm in the present tense ("a renderer reads the spec default, it never keeps a page size of its own"); at the pin that is the ruling, not the shipped state. It reads as the contract's requirement, which is what a schema docblock is for.
- **One objectui text still states 25 as the spec default.** `objectql.zod.ts:143` docblock: "the spec's `.default(25)` is stripped at the import boundary". The PR body's "No objectui test pins 25 as the spec default" is true but narrower than the sweep it implies; objectui is read-only for this card, so the correction belongs to objectui#9853 (noted under ③).

### ② Semver level

- **`minor` for `@objectstack/spec` is right.** No accept-set change, no removal, no new key, no type change; a behaviour change for every author who omits the key, so not `patch`. `.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml:753-766` ("WHICH LEVEL") grades a widening at least `minor` and leaves the two sub-major levels to the act; `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` refuses `major` in the launch window. Precedent for a published-default move: `.changeset/enableoninstall-optional-preserve.md` and `.changeset/18605-enable-on-install-one-authority.md`, both `'@objectstack/spec': minor`. `Check Changeset` concluded `success` on the head.
- **`Clause-②: no` is the right declaration.** Clause ② is "a new key on a published payload" (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs:7-8`); a moved default adds no key, so the level axis stands down. The changeset carries no BREAKING banner, so `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` judges nothing and no ADR-0087 `registered` marker is owed (script header lines 51-60: the gate is driven off the changeset's own breaking declaration).
- **`DEFAULT_CHANGES_BY_MAJOR` row: demanded by the build, and truthful.** `packages/spec/scripts/lib/default-changes.ts:537-539` (`ui/PaginationConfig:pageSize`, `from '25'`, `to '50'`) sits under `17`, which is `CURRENT_MAJOR` (spec `17.4.0`; `build-schemas.ts:955`), the only bucket that authorises anything (header lines 25-26). The header (lines 11-12) says `check:authorable-surface` refuses any default move until it is declared here, so this file was not optional. `from` and `to` are re-derived from the merge-base fingerprint and the build's emission, so the row cannot be wrong without the gate going red; its `reason` states what moves and the one-line way to keep 25, which is what the header asks for (lines 43-49). The `authorable-defaults.test.ts:410-421` self-test's constraints (from differs from to, reason longer than 20 characters, key shape) are met.
- **Semantic entry `view-pagination-page-size-default-50`: warranted, correctly filed, accurate.** Warrant: `default-changes.ts:51-55` prescribes a semantic entry for a default change "that also warrants a migration TODO", and this one reaches deployed documents silently: the objectql engine registers the PARSED body of every assembled `viewItems:` entry (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts:6574`, `:6589`, `:6596`), and the probe shows `AssembledViewArtifactSchema` with a list overlay carrying `pagination: {}` parsing to `pageSize` 25 before and 50 after. Filing at step 18 for a 17.x change: correct per `registry.ts:4773-4783` ("v17.0.0 was cut before these narrowings landed, so their migration prescriptions belong to the NEXT major ... The enforcement itself ships earlier on the 17.x line ... this step is where `migrate meta` users are told"); precedent `data/Field:unique` (row under 17 at `default-changes.ts:365`, entry `18.autonumber-default-unique-organization.ts`). Content: every sentence of `reason` and `acceptanceCriteria` (`18.view-pagination-page-size-default-50.ts:17-36`) matches the probe (empty config to 50, `pagination: {}` on a list view to 50, authored 25 stays 25, 0 / negative / fraction refused, absent stays absent); `surface` (line 14) carries no backtick, as its own comment and `build-upgrade-guide.ts` require, and a surface with spaces and a dash has 37 precedents in the registry. It tells an upgrading deployment the one true thing a mechanical pass cannot decide: which silent views were relying on 25. Not noise.
- **Registry regeneration.** `registry.ts:14062` places the entry in id order between `view-filter-rule-scalar-operator-array-refused` and `wait-node-event-config-required`, with the entry file's leading `//` comment carried verbatim, which is what `build-migration-registry.ts` (sorted by id, comment run copied) emits per `entries/README.md`. Step-18 ids are not projected: `packages/spec/docs/protocol-upgrade-guide.md` and `packages/spec/spec-changes.json` at the head contain no step-18 id (0 hits for three of them), so "gen:spec-changes and gen:upgrade-guide produced zero diff" is right. Whether the regions match byte-for-byte is `check:migration-registry`'s call and is left to the head's check-runs (not rerun here).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **CLI scaffold `pagination: { pageSize: 25 }` (`packages/cli/src/commands/generate.ts:164`).** Answer: an authored value, validates, parses to 25 on both sides; not a defect under this card. But it now scaffolds the OLD number rather than the platform default, so every `os generate view` output silently pins 25 rows where the ruling says 50. Worth a follow-up card (drop the key, or write 50); carrier none today, as the dev noted.
- **Stored views with `pagination: {}` change visible row count on upgrade, by channel.** (a) Tenant-authored / runtime-assembled views travel in `viewItems:` and the engine registers the parsed body (`engine.ts:6574-6596`), so such a view is served with `pageSize: 50` materialised (was 25) and the Console honours a served `pagination.pageSize` (`ObjectGrid.tsx:1231`, `ListView.tsx:1307`): those views show 50 rows on upgrade with no objectui change. (b) Stack-authored `views:` containers register without a full `ViewSchema.parse` (`engine.ts:6521` comment) and objectui strips the default, so a `pagination: {}` container view keeps the renderer's own number (grid 10, list 100, kanban 100) until objectui#9853. The PR body does not separate the two channels; the changeset's "pagination block without pageSize now shows 50 rows" is exact for (a) and lands for (b) only with objectui#9853. Not blocking: the contract statement is correct on both, and the semantic entry already tells the deployment to write `pageSize: 25` where 25 was relied on.
- **No server-side consumer reads the parsed default as a query limit.** `git grep` for `pagination?.pageSize` / `pagination.pageSize` outside `packages/spec`, non-test, at the head: zero hits. No REST list limit or engine path derives from this default. Right.
- **Spec describe vs the renderer's plan for non-paged views.** The card's Unblocks section says objectui#9853 keeps "a renamed fetch batch of 100" for non-paged views and kanban, while the unchanged describe (`view.zod.ts:1110-1112`) says `pageSize` is the fetch ceiling on a view with no pager. Pre-existing, not moved by this PR; objectui#9853 should reconcile which number a silent kanban actually fetches (50 per the spec default, or its own 100).
- **objectui residual text.** `packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts:143` still says `.default(25)`; objectui#9853 should update it when it lands the renderer side.
- **Check-runs on the head, final snapshot at hand-back (per check, latest run).** 27 concluded `success` (including Check Changeset, Type Check · source gates, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Documentation Links, the single-writer and claim guards); skipped: Auto Label, Check PR Size, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in); still `in_progress` at hand-back: Lint & Repo Gates, Test Core (1/6), Test Core (5/6); non-success conclusions: none. The verdict below is conditional on the in-progress families concluding `success`; a `failure` among them re-opens this record.

**VERDICT: PASS**
